note: V18 (Amenti.live, Ingram Manor: the board at 50,000 ft over Cape Canaveral), 28 Nov 2026: the view below the horizon, painted. Claude joins the three wide takes round the compass and lays the straight-down painting under the board; the sky above stays live.
style: A luminous, realistic painting in the manner of Robert McCall's NASA and aviation art: precise, atmospheric, airy, painted with care for real light and real cloud. Seen from 50,000 feet (15 km) above Florida's Atlantic coast, looking out and down. The horizon is perfectly level and sits very high, one tenth of the way down from the top of the picture, a soft pale haze line; above it only a thin band of deep blue sky. Everything below the horizon is the view down through the atmosphere: varied cloud at many heights, low cumulus fields and long parallel cloud streets, mid-level altocumulus patches, high thin cirrus streaks casting soft shadows, hazy stretches opening into clear gaps, the ground and sea seen through them far below. Soft even midday light from high above, no sun disc in the picture. One single continuous canvas filling the whole frame edge to edge: not a triptych, not panels, no gaps, no white margins, no letterbox bars, no photograph of a canvas. The left and right edges continue naturally into more of the same view so the pictures can be joined side by side. No aircraft, no rockets, no people, no text, no signature, no frame, no border.

beats.text: Looking west over Cape Canaveral: the long white Atlantic beaches, the Cape's point, Merritt Island and the broad dark lagoons of the Banana River and the Indian River behind it, the green and tan Florida land beyond fading into haze toward the horizon, the tiny geometric launch pads on the coast. Cloud streets drift across the view at different heights, with clear gaps.

Looking east over the open Atlantic Ocean: deep blue water far below, long rows of low fair-weather cumulus in cloud streets, patches of higher altocumulus, wisps of cirrus, haze thickening toward the horizon. No land.

Looking north along Florida's Atlantic coast: the thin bright line of beach between the blue ocean on the right and the green land and lagoons on the left, running away toward the horizon into haze, with layered cloud between: cumulus fields low, thin cirrus high above them.

Looking straight down from 50,000 feet onto the coast just east of Cape Canaveral: the deep blue Atlantic, a scatter of small low cumulus clouds with their shadows on the water, a few soft high cirrus wisps above them. No horizon; the picture is entirely the view vertically down. The same scale and light as the other paintings.
